business_problem: BNP Paribas Global Markets sales teams were manually interpreting client requests for quotes from chat and email and filling response forms on a dedicated platform, which took several minutes per quote and made speed and reliability difficult at high volume.
solution_summary: BNP Paribas built Chat2Trade as an internal AI workflow for its Global Markets business to turn unstructured RFQ text into a structured format that downstream pricing systems can use. The system ingests client requests arriving through chat or email, extracts the plain text, and passes it to a pre-trained open-source BERT language model that BNP Paribas fine-tuned internally using historical client requests and synthetic data generated from templates. The model performs text classification and named entity recognition so the request can be understood and tagged with the relevant product characteristics. Those outputs are assembled into a final structured output format and handed off to internal pricing tools, which then generate the quote for sales teams to return to clients. BNP Paribas says the deployment is fully rolled out, closely monitored, and updated with new model versions almost every week.
